title: Muscles moving the arm: biceps and triceps
subject: Life science

sources.title: NGSS MS-LS1-3: Use argument supported by evidence for how the body is a system of interacting subsystems composed of groups of cells
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.1 Interactions of Skeletal Muscles

legend.name: Muscle
legend.meaning: Red, because it's full of blood vessels

note.text: Bones are levers. Muscles move them by pulling.
The forearm has two bones. They meet the upper arm bone at the elbow, a joint that bends.

steps.title: Biceps
steps.instruction: Trace the biceps on the front of the upper arm.

note.text: When the biceps contracts, it gets shorter and pulls the forearm up, bending the elbow.

steps.title: Biceps tendon
steps.instruction: Draw the tendon joining the biceps to the forearm.

note.text: Tendons are strong bands that join muscles to bones. They pass the muscle's pull to the bone.

steps.title: Triceps
steps.instruction: Trace the triceps on the back of the upper arm.

note.text: When the triceps contracts, it pulls the forearm down, straightening the elbow.

steps.title: Triceps tendon
steps.instruction: Draw the tendon joining the triceps to the forearm.

note.text: It attaches just behind the elbow, so its pull straightens the arm.

steps.title: Lifting
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow showing the forearm lifting.

note.text: Nerves signal the biceps to contract. Nervous, muscular and skeletal systems all work together to move.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: Color the bones and the muscles.

steps.title: Name the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the name for each numbered part.

mistakes.Triceps: The triceps is on the back of the arm. This front muscle is the biceps.

steps.title: Pairs
steps.question: Muscles can pull but can't push. So how do you straighten your arm again after bending it?

options.text: The triceps contracts and pulls the forearm back down
options.feedback: Yes. Muscles work in opposing pairs: the biceps bends the elbow, the triceps straightens it.
Muscles can only pull. The triceps does the straightening.
Bones can't move on their own. The triceps pulls them.
Tendons only pass on a muscle's pull. The triceps pulls the arm straight.

steps.title: Systems
steps.instruction: Think about all the systems involved.
steps.question: Which body systems work together when you lift a glass of water?

options.text: Nervous, muscular and skeletal, with blood bringing the muscles energy
options.feedback: Right. Nerves signal, muscles pull, bones move, and the circulatory system fuels the muscles.
Muscles need nerve signals to contract and bones to pull on.
Bones can't move on their own. Muscles and nerves are needed too.
Digestion supplies energy over time, but nerves, muscles and bones do the lifting.
